- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizon.
- After a price spike (forecast > 82.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.10), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for 1–2 day horizon.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is > 80.0, reduce by 1–2% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 1–3 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; adjust downward by 1–3% for short-term.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.30 correlates with forecast error; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7 * sentiment + 0.3 * historical) for correction.
